correctness.rationale: Because propositional truth is unchanged when the update only adds accessibility arrows, a row with successor set \(S\) and truth set \(P\) evolves by \(c_P(S)=S\cup P^c\) when \(S\subseteq P\) and is otherwise fixed. After an active update the row either is unchanged because \(P^c\) is empty or contains a counterexample, so a second identical update is inactive. For two truth sets, direct case analysis proves commutation when \(P=Q\) or \(P\cup Q=W\). If both fail, the empty row is sent to distinct complements in the two orders. Two propositional valuations realize the formula-level countermodel, and a fresh marker atom distinguishes the resulting relations. The frozen exhaustive checker through six worlds independently matches the arbitrary-set proof.
correctness.risk: The theorem depends essentially on propositional contents; modal contents can change truth value after the edge update.

value.rationale: Repetition and order are basic structural questions for a dynamic belief-change operation. The theorem gives a complete simplification law for factual contractions and a minimal two-world obstruction when order matters, making the result both mathematically sharp and directly usable in reasoning about contraction sequences.
value.risk: The structural law does not extend automatically to modal contraction contents.

final_claim: For Belardinelli-Zhang hedged public-announcement contraction by propositional contents, every contraction is idempotent, and two contractions commute on every Kripke model exactly when their propositional contents are classically equivalent or their disjunction is tautological.
limitations: Universal model-level commutation is stronger than accidental commutation on one fixed relation.
No claim is made for contraction mixed with expansion or revision.
